issues.legal_issue: A widow who receives her deceased husband's interest in undivided joint-family property under the statutory widow's-rights regime has a coparcenary interest and is a member of the coparcenary, though she is not herself a coparcener.
material_facts: The deceased husband had been a member of a Mitakshara Hindu coparcenary, and his widow acquired his interest in the joint-family property under the statutory widow's-rights regime.
The widow had the same right as her husband to seek partition, but she did not seek partition before her death.
The widow's interest involved common possession and enjoyment with the other members and fluctuated with changes in the family and its property.
issues.conclusion: The widow possessed a coparcenary interest and was a member of the coparcenary, although she was not a coparcener in the strict legal sense.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(2) of the Hindu Women's Rights to Property Act, 1937 gave the widow the same interest her husband had, and section 3(3) limited that interest to a Hindu woman's estate while giving her the same right to claim partition as a male owner. Applying the incidents of Mitakshara coparcenary described in State Bank of India v. Ghamandi Ram, the Court held that the widow possessed the relevant coparcenary indicia apart from acquiring an interest by birth. The Court also relied on Jaisri Sahu v. Rajdewan Dubey, Potti Lakshmi Perumallu v. Potti Krishnavenamma, Satrughan Isser v. Smt. Subujpari, Parappagari Parappa v. Parappagari Nagamma, Smt. Sabujpari v. Satrughan Isser, and Mst. Khatrani Kuer v. Smt. Tapeshwari Kuer.

rule.if: estate_duty_proceeding and widow_received_husbands_joint_family_interest and widow_had_right_to_seek_partition and widow_shared_undivided_property

predicates.estate_duty_proceeding: The proceeding concerned whether an interest in joint-family property was included in an estate for estate-duty purposes.
predicates.widow_received_husbands_joint_family_int: A widow received the interest her deceased husband had held in joint-family property.
predicates.widow_had_right_to_seek_partition: The widow had the right to seek partition of the joint-family property on the same basis as her husband.
predicates.widow_shared_undivided_property: Before partition, the widow shared possession and enjoyment of the property with the other family members.

issues.definition: When an estate-duty proceeding concerns a widow who received her husband's joint-family interest, could seek partition, and shared undivided property with the family, the rule treats her as holding a coparcenary interest and being a member, but not a coparcener.

issues.legal_issue: A widow's coparcenary interest in joint-family property that ends when she dies without seeking partition is deemed to pass on her death and is liable to estate duty, with its value determined by the share she would have received on an immediate partition.
material_facts: The widow held an interest in joint-family property derived from her deceased husband.
She died without seeking partition, while the coparcenary property remained undivided.
The value of her share could be determined by calculating what would have been allotted to her on a partition immediately before her death.
issues.conclusion: The widow's interest ceased on her death and merged into the coparcenary property; it was deemed to pass on her death and was liable to estate duty, valued by reference to the share she would have received on an immediate partition.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 7(1) and 7(2) of the Estate Duty Act, 1953 cover a coparcenary interest in joint-family property that ceases on death, and section 39 provides for valuing the benefit by reference to the share that would have been allotted on a partition immediately before death. The Court distinguished Attorney-General of Ceylon v. Arunachalam Chettiar and Gartside v. Inland Revenue Commissioners because the statutory provisions and the widow's interest in this case differed. It accepted that fiscal statutes are construed strictly, but held that the statutory language must be given effect where it covers the taxable interest.

rule.if: estate_duty_proceeding and widow_held_joint_family_interest and widow_died_without_seeking_partition and property_remained_undivided and share_determinable_on_assumed_partition

predicates.estate_duty_proceeding: The proceeding concerned whether an interest in joint-family property was included in an estate for estate-duty purposes.
predicates.widow_held_joint_family_interest: A widow held an interest in joint-family property derived from her deceased husband.
predicates.widow_died_without_seeking_partition: The widow died without having sought partition of the joint-family property.
predicates.property_remained_undivided: The joint-family property had not been partitioned before the widow's death.
predicates.share_determinable_on_assumed_partition: The widow's share could be calculated by determining what she would have received if the property had been partitioned immediately before her death.

issues.definition: When an estate-duty proceeding concerns a widow's interest in undivided joint-family property, and she dies without seeking partition while her share remains determinable by an assumed immediate partition, the rule treats her interest as passing on death and chargeable to estate duty.
